kicker: Restaurants & cafés · same-store sales growth, Q2 FY27
title: Same-store sales rose at 11 of 12 restaurant brands
dek: Outlets open a year or more drew more diners, not higher bills: Devyani and Jubilant raised menu prices only 1–2% this year, while food inflation hit 8.94% in October.

chart.title: Same-store sales growth (SSSG), Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: India brands, as stated on Q2 calls · SSSG = sales growth at outlets open a year or more

stats.label: Median same-store growth
stats.note: Across 12 brands; the 11 with a Q1 figure: +7.1% in Q1, +8.1% in Q2.

stats.label: Menu price rises this year
stats.note: Devyani; Jubilant took 1.4–2%. Barbeque Nation has not raised prices in four quarters.

read: Old outlets, not just new ones, drove Q2; with food costs rising near 9%, the test is whether chains can raise prices without losing those diners.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; food inflation: Liquide, 13 Nov 2026
notes: Same-store sales growth (SSSG: sales growth at outlets open a year or more, which strips out new openings) is as each company stated it on its Q2 FY27 call, for India brands only, year on year; Q1 FY27 figures come from the Q1 calls (Burger King's and Speciality's as restated on the Q2 call). Tiles are green where SSSG is at or above October CPI food inflation of 8.94% (Liquide, 13 Nov 2026), saffron where positive but below it and red where negative; restaurant menu inflation is not the same as food CPI, so the threshold is a reference, not a measure of real growth. Navratri fell in October this year against September last year, which lifts Q2 for chicken and meat brands: Sapphire put the effect at about 4–5 points on KFC and guided to high single-digit KFC SSSG for Q2 and Q3 combined, so Q3 will be weaker for these brands. Growth was transaction-led: over 50% of Sapphire's KFC SSSG came from more orders, Westlife reported double-digit guest count growth, and Barbeque Nation's average realisation fell about 7–8% with no price rise in four quarters. Toscano and Salt belong to United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation's parent). Westlife guided to 2–4% price rises over the year and Sapphire cited 2–3% in Q1, so pricing is not uniform. Store counts: Devyani added 70 net, Sapphire 16, Westlife 11 and Barbeque Nation 9 restaurants in Q2. Jubilant FoodWorks is left out of the grid because its Q2 call data gives no Domino's LFL figure (it guides 5–7% for the full year; Q1 was 2.5%); Costa has no Q1 figure; international units (Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Barbeque Nation abroad, Turkey) are excluded.
